title: Kentucky: history overview
d: Kentucky: the Bluegrass State, admitted 1792 (15th); capital Frankfort.
definition: Kentucky: the Bluegrass State, admitted 1792 (15th); capital Frankfort.
description: Kentucky — "Bluegrass State" — entered the Union 1792 (15th). Its capital is Frankfort and its largest city is Louisville. Shawnee hunting grounds; Daniel Boone. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Kentucky achieved statehood 1792 (15th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Civil War border state. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Kentucky its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Kentucky went from territory to state.
definition: How Kentucky went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Kentucky: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Bourbon, horses, coal. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Kentucky's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Frankfort
d: Frankfort is the capital of Kentucky.
definition: Frankfort is the capital of Kentucky.
description: Frankfort has been the seat of Kentucky government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Kentucky's largest is Louisville — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Bluegrass State
description: The nickname "Bluegrass State" captures how Kentucky sees itself — and how America sees it. The Kentucky Derby has run every year since 1875. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "United we stand, divided we fall."

title: Motto: United we stand, divided we fall
t: Motto: United we stand, divided we fall
d: The state motto of Kentucky is "United we stand, divided we fall."
definition: The state motto of Kentucky is "United we stand, divided we fall."
description: The motto "United we stand, divided we fall" is Kentucky's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Seal with two men shaking hands on blue. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
